title: Eighteen meters better
objective: Apply the ERS/ATS technical standard when interpreting 6-minute walk results: a 30 m change is the smallest difference that counts as clinically meaningful
secondaryObjectives: Titrate supplemental oxygen to target saturations: 94% to 98% for most patients, 88% to 92% for those at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure, such as COPD

brief.situation: 09:00 in an outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation gym. You are the physical therapist. Mrs. Lindqvist, 72, with COPD, is in her last week. Her discharge 6-minute walk yesterday was 328 m against 310 m at intake, on the same course and her same ordered oxygen. The program manager has drafted a letter to her pulmonologist and insurer saying she 'achieved a clinically meaningful improvement' and wants you to sign it. Meanwhile she is cycling an interval.
handover: Her oxygen order: titrate to a saturation of 88-92%; she is at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure.
Program policy: outcome reports go to the referring pulmonologist; the physical therapist signs the functional results.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Is Mrs. Lindqvist's walk result a clinically meaningful improvement, and what do you report?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: No: +18 m on the same course and oxygen is below the ERS/ATS 30 m smallest meaningful change, though she reports real day-to-day gains; today she also desaturated below her 88-92% target on exertion.
parts.modelAnswer: No. 18 m is under the 30 m that counts as meaningful, even though she feels she's doing more. And she dropped below 88% on the bike today.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Ease the load until she recovers; decline to sign the letter as drafted; send an accurate report with the distance, the threshold, her day-to-day gains and today's desaturation; document.
parts.modelAnswer: Back off the bike till she's back in range, don't sign the letter as written, and send an honest report with all of it.

scoring.modelReasoning: The ERS/ATS technical standard puts the smallest clinically meaningful change in 6-minute walk distance at 30 m, so +18 m on the same course and oxygen is not a clinically meaningful improvement, whatever the percentage. Report it accurately alongside her own day-to-day gains. During exercise, keep her at her 88-92% target as someone at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure: ease off when she falls below it.
